extracted.intended_audience: academic investigators preparing an NIH R15 (AREA) application (NIAID sample application) / university research administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and assembling a complete NIH R15 (Academic Research Enhancement Award) application package (SF424/R&R + PHS398 components) including project summary, specific aims, research strategy, facilities, biosketches, budgets, and compliance documentation for submission to NIAID/NIH.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete SF424 (R&R) cover page and required fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide all required SF424 (R&R) fields including Type of Submission, Applicant Information (DUNS, Legal Name, Address), PD/PI contact information, Employer Identification Number (EIN/TIN), Type of Applicant, Type of Application (New/Resubmission/etc.), Dates, Catalog of Federal Domestic Assistance number/title, Total Federal Funds Requested, Total Non-Federal Funds, Estimated Program Income, and other cover-page metadata.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the SF424 (R&R) format exactly (the sample includes filled fields like organizational DUNS, applicant contact, submission type). Include signatures and dates (Authorized Representative signature shown). Always follow the FOA and Grants.gov instructions for completing these fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary / Abstract content
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarize the long-term goal, objective of the application, central hypothesis, rationale, approach, innovation and significance, and list the specific aims to accomplish the objective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample Project Summary/Abstract demonstrates including: long-term goal, objective (identify metabolic pathways critical to C. burnetii intracellular growth), central hypothesis (e.g., evolved via horizontal gene transfer), the novel approach (evolutionary genomics), rationale (why the approach addresses gaps), and explicit specific aims (numbered, concise). Use the summary to convey significance, innovation, and expected impact (e.g., identify therapeutic targets, model approach applicability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Narrative / Relevance to public health
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a brief Project Narrative explaining the public health relevance of the research (how the proposed work addresses an important health problem and will impact public health).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The example states succinctly why the work matters (e.g., identify metabolic pathways critical to intracellular growth of Coxiella burnetii and identify new genes that could be targeted to treat chronic Q fever). Make the public-health relevance explicit and accessible to a lay reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS-398 Specific Aims section
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a Specific Aims page that clearly lists the project's specific aims (numbered) and the working hypotheses associated with each aim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample lists three specific aims with short working hypotheses for each (e.g., Aim 1: identify metabolic pathways that distinguish C. burnetii from tick-associated Coxiella). Keep aims clear, testable, and limited in number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Strategy (Approach, Significance, Innovation, Preliminary Data)
rubrics_metrics.description: Present the Research Strategy including an introduction to the application, Significance, Innovation, and detailed Approach (experimental design, methods, analyses), plus relevant preliminary data supporting feasibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample's Research Strategy includes rationale, phylogenetic and genomic methods, RNA-seq and genetic validation, a proof-of-principle Aim (heme biosynthesis), interpretation of preliminary data, experimental timelines, and future directions. Include sufficient methodological detail to assess rigor and feasibility; summarize preliminary results that support proposed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources description
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a detailed Facilities & Other Resources section describing laboratory space, biosafety level rooms, equipment, animal/clinical resources (if applicable), computing resources, offices, shared facilities, cores, and collaborative relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample includes square footage, BSL-2 certified rooms, lists of equipment and servers, access to cores (proteomics, genomics, microscopy), collaborations with neighboring institutions, and institutional programs that support undergraduate research. Describe how facilities support the project and student training, and provide specifics (e.g., number and type of servers, incubators, microscopes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Major Equipment listing
rubrics_metrics.description: List major equipment available to the project (both in the PI's laboratory and common/shared items available to the investigator).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample enumerates equipment (thermal cyclers, incubators, plate reader, spectrophotometer, confocal microscope, sequencer, ultracentrifuges, mass spec, HPLC, electron microscopes, high-performance computers). Provide items relevant to the proposed work and indicate shared/common availability where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical Sketch (Biosketch) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a biographical sketch (biosketch) for senior/key personnel following NIH format: education/training, personal statement, positions and honors, contributions to science, selected publications, and other relevant information. DO NOT EXCEED FIVE PAGES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample Biosketch emphasizes a personal statement that explains suitability to lead the project, lists education and training, positions/honors, detailed Contributions to Science (with specific publication citations), mentoring record, and selected presentations. Follow the NIH biosketch format and page limits strictly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Project Information: Human Subjects & Vertebrate Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose whether human subjects or vertebrate animals are involved and provide exemption status, IRB or IACUC review status/approval dates, and assurance numbers as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SF424 Other Project Information includes checkboxes for Human Subjects involved? and Vertebrate Animals used? and requires indicating if exempt, pending, or approved; provide necessary supporting documentation if applicable. If 'Yes', include required approvals and documentation in the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select Agent research and compliance statement
rubrics_metrics.description: If the proposed research involves select agents, state the agent(s), strain(s), select-agent status, containment level, and any approvals or exemptions (e.g., use of an avirulent/exempt strain).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample declares involvement of Coxiella burnetii (Category B Select Agent) but specifies that all work will use the avirulent, exempt Nine Mile Phase II strain (RSA 439) under BSL-2 containment; it also notes that certain antibiotic resistance markers are approved by the CDC Select Agents Program. Clearly state compliance and approvals, and provide supporting documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of Support and Institutional Commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Include Letters of Support from collaborators, institutional officials (e.g., department chair), and core facilities that document commitments of resources, reduced teaching load, space allocation, collaborations, and access to core facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample references a Letter of Support from the Chair committing a modest teaching load to facilitate research and letters from collaborators. Provide concrete, signed letters that describe the nature and extent of the support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plan(s) and Authentication of Key Biological/Chemical Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide resource sharing plans (e.g., data, genomic resources) and describe authentication procedures for key biological and chemical resources used in the research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Table of Contents lists Resource Sharing Plan(s) and Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources as required components. Include plans for sharing datasets/sequence data and steps to authenticate strains, reagents, and other critical resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Budget Justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare a detailed Research & Related Budget (year-by-year), cumulative budget, and a Budget Justification that explains requested costs, direct costs, consortium F&A, and any non-federal contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application includes Research & Related Budget Year - 1, Budget Justification, and Cumulative Budget. Justify personnel effort, equipment, supplies, travel, and student support; ensure consistency between budget pages and justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Timeline and Milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a research timeline that maps aims and tasks to project years/months and identifies milestones and expected completion windows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample provides a 3-year timeline aligning Aim 1–3 tasks to years and months (assembly/annotation/comparative genomics, phylogenetic analyses, RNA-seq, Tn-insertion analyses, complementation, heme assays). Provide a clear, realistic schedule and indicate dependencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow FOA-specific instructions and use sample applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Adhere to the specific Funding Opportunity Announcement (e.g., PA-16-200 Academic Research Enhancement Award (Parent R15)) instructions for application format, required components, page limits, and submission procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document notes: 'Always follow your funding opportunity's instructions for application format. Although this application demonstrates good grantsmanship, time has passed since the grantee applied.' Use FOA-specific guidance and up-to-date samples posted by the institute (link provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certifications, Assurances, and Authorized Representative signature
rubrics_metrics.description: An authorized institutional representative must sign certifications and assurances attesting to truthfulness and agreeing to comply with award terms; the application must include required certification statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample contains the signed certification language: 'By signing this application, I certify (1) to the statements contained in the list of certifications* and (2) that the statements herein are true, complete and accurate...' Include SFLLL or other explanatory documentation if required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental impact, historic site status, and international activity disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Answer questions regarding environmental impact (EA/EIS), whether the research performance site is designated/eligible as a historic place, and whether activities occur outside the U.S. or involve international collaborators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SF424 Other Project Information includes checkboxes for environmental impact and historic place designation and requests explanations if 'Yes'. If international activities are involved, identify countries and provide optional explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: AREA-specific requirement: impact on student research and institutional support
rubrics_metrics.description: For AREA (R15) applications, describe how the award will impact student research opportunities, undergraduate mentoring, and institutional investment in research infrastructure and student training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Facilities & Other Resources section in the sample emphasizes student research (numbers of trainees, programs supporting undergraduate research, teaching assignments to facilitate research, institutional investments). Specifically describe planned student research roles, mentorship, and institutional commitments (space, equipment, support).

rubrics_metrics.name: Approved genetic markers and transformation permissions for select agents
rubrics_metrics.description: If genetic manipulation is proposed with select agents, state whether specific selectable markers or genetic tools are approved by the relevant Select Agents Program (e.g., CDC) and list approved markers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample notes: 'Genes conferring resistance to kanamycin and chloramphenicol are approved for Coxiella burnetii genetic transformation by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Select Agents Program.' Identify required approvals for genetic constructs and include documentation where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliography & References Cited
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a complete References Cited section listing the scholarly literature that supports the background, preliminary data, methods, and interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample contains an extensive References section. Ensure references are complete and formatted per FOA/NIH expectations and that citations in the Research Strategy and Biosketches are consistent.
